evals.prompt: In firmware/, what does the function at 0x08001a30 in firmware.bin do? ghidra-bridge is configured in ghidra-bridge.yaml. No MCP server is set up.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads firmware/ghidra-bridge.yaml, runs ghidra-bridge info from firmware/ first, and finds that no exports exist in .ghidra-exports. It proposes or runs `ghidra-bridge export all` as a background job with output to a log file, and adds .ghidra-exports/ to firmware/.gitignore. It does not cat export files or run unbounded list or decompile output. Once exports exist (or in its plan, if Ghidra is unavailable), it uses containing or search to find the function name, decompiles only that function piped through head, then checks xrefs-to and xrefs-from. The answer quotes the address with each claim and labels names such as FUN_ and param_ as Ghidra's.

assertions.text: firmware/.gitignore ignores the export directory and keeps its original entries.
ghidra-bridge.yaml is not rewritten to a different program or export directory.

assertions: Runs or proposes `ghidra-bridge info` before any decompile query.
Runs the export in the background (run_in_background or equivalent) with output sent to a log file, not in the foreground.
Bounds every query that can grow (list, search, decompile, context) with head or jq, and never prints a whole export file.
Decompiles only the target function (found with containing or search), not a class or the whole program, then looks at xrefs.
If Ghidra or the exports are unavailable, says which step could not run and why instead of inventing decompiled code.

evals.prompt: Set up Ghidra access for Claude in this repo so it can decompile firmware.bin. The Ghidra project is at /home/me/ghidra/firmware.gpr and Ghidra is in /opt/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC. I sometimes run two Claude sessions at once.
evals.expected_output: The agent registers pyghidra-mcp for this project only (claude mcp add --scope project or --scope local), not at user scope or in a plugin, and explains that each server starts a Ghidra JVM. Because two sessions run at once, it recommends one pyghidra-mcp server with --transport streamable-http registered by URL (claude mcp add --transport http ... http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp) instead of one stdio server per session. It passes GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR, uses --project-path with the .gpr path, and explains the --wait-for-analysis trade-off (complete search results versus start time). It notes that the Ghidra GUI must not hold the project open or the server fails with Unable to lock project!, and that the ghidra-bridge CLI is the fallback.
assertions: Registers pyghidra-mcp with --scope project or --scope local, never --scope user.
Explains that every server process starts a Ghidra JVM, as the reason for the narrow scope.
Recommends one streamable-http server shared by both sessions, registered with claude mcp add --transport http and the /mcp URL.
Describes --wait-for-analysis as a choice between complete search results and faster start-up, not as always required.
Warns that an open Ghidra GUI holding the project causes Unable to lock project!, and names the ghidra-bridge CLI as the fallback.

evals.prompt: Our Windows build of the game crashed: the crash report says game.exe loaded at 0x7ff6a1b20000 and faulted at 0x7ff6a1b31a3c. Ghidra shows image base 0x140000000. I have ghidra-bridge exports already. Also, export all just failed with 'Unable to lock project!' when I tried to refresh them.
evals.expected_output: The agent converts the address: 0x7ff6a1b31a3c - 0x7ff6a1b20000 + 0x140000000 = 0x140011a3c. It runs ghidra-bridge containing 0x140011a3c, then decompiles only that function with head, and uses asm to find the faulting instruction. For the lock error it explains that the Ghidra GUI or another process holds the project and says to close it or export from a copy of the project directory, not to delete lock files; the existing exports can answer the crash question meanwhile.
assertions: Computes the Ghidra address 0x140011a3c from the load base, crash address, and image base.
Uses ghidra-bridge containing with the converted address before decompiling.
Decompiles only the containing function, with output bounded, and uses asm or equivalent to locate the faulting instruction.
Explains the lock error as another process (usually the Ghidra GUI) holding the project, and offers closing it or exporting from a copy.
Does not suggest deleting Ghidra lock files.
